akn: B. Antieau, A. Krause, T. Nikolaus, On the K-theory of Z/p^n, arXiv:2405.04329
conventions: One entry per ring R = O_K/pi^n = W(F_q)[z]/(E(z), z^n), with W(F_q) = Z_p[x]/(htilde) and E Eisenstein of degree e; htilde lists its coefficients from low to high degree, and E[k+1] the coordinates of the coefficient of z^k in the basis 1, x, ..., x^(f-1). groups: for every degree 1 <= r <= 100 the p-adic K-group K_r(R; Z_p) = sum_j Z/p^{a_j}, as the sorted list of its exponents [a_1, ...] ([] is the zero group); K_0(R; Z_p) = Z_p is not listed. status: for the rings of [AKN, Appendix A] "printed" if the group is printed there (it agrees with the computed one), "x" if [AKN] mark the degree x (not computed within 48 hours), "beyond" if the degree lies after the last row of their table; for the other rings "hesselholt_madsen" if n <= e, so that R = F_q[z]/z^n and the group agrees with Hesselholt and Madsen's, and "not_in_akn" otherwise. new is true for "x", "beyond" and "not_in_akn". The integral groups are K_r(R) = K_r(R; Z_p) + Z/(q^i - 1) for r = 2i - 1 and K_r(R) = K_r(R; Z_p) for even r >= 2 [AKN, Section 1.1, p. 2].
